subject: Discovery Recap: Reliability & Graceful Degradation - Acme Health
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmehealth.io>, Evan Liu <evan.liu@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap: Reliability & Graceful Degradation - Acme Health

Hi Sophie / Evan -

Thanks again for carving out 30 minutes today - really helpful to understand Acme Health's reliability constraints and recent incidents. Per our call, below is a concise recap so we have aligned next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

High-level pain points
- Production incidents in Q1 2026 caused increased latency and partial feature degradation for the patient triage flow (most notable: 2026-01-15 incident, ~45 minutes of elevated 95th percentile latency).
- Current stack: in-house model serving on cloud VMs with manual failover; no automated model fallback and limited cross-region routing.
- Cache misses during peak windows make response times highly variable.

Primary goals / success criteria
- Achieve p95 latency <= 300ms for patient triage happy path under our test load (SLO target).
- Reduce incident MTTR to < 15 minutes for inference availability degradations via automated fallback policies.
- Graceful degradation behavior: when capacity constrained or region degraded, fallback to smaller model variant or cached/templated response with clear telemetry and rate-limited degradation path.

Incident history (from our discussion)
- 2026-01-15: downstream storage async queue spike -> sustained high token latencies (~45m). Root cause: autoscaling lag + cold KV caches.
- 2025-11-03: region outage affecting a subset of requests; manual route changes required.

What Redwood can help with (initial ideas)
- Dedicated pools + cross-region routing for predictable throughput and automated region fallback.
- Built-in model variants and automatic fallback (e.g., run smaller quantized model when primary variant overloaded).
- Prefix/KV caching to cut tail latency and reduce costs; quality-aware cached responses for non-critical paths.
- SLO/SLA proposal and runbook playbooks for graceful degradation and incident automation.

Suggested next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/plat-engineering (we recommend involving one of your SREs) - 60 min. Proposed slots: Thu 26 Feb 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 27 Feb 14:00-15:00 PT. Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/chloe-tech-deep-dive
2) I will share a short pilot proposal and an initial mutual-action plan for a Dedicated pilot (attached: rwi-pilot-proposal.pdf).
3) If you can, please share the incident postmortem for 2026-01-15 and any SLO targets you currently track (attached stubs OK).

Attachments: rwi-pilot-proposal.pdf (proposal + threading plan), rwi-discovery-note.pdf (notes from today's call)

Thanks - I'll coordinate with Marcus and Marissa on the technical follow-up.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acmehealth.io>

Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@acmehealth.io>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Reliability & Graceful Degradation - Acme Health

Chloe -

Thanks for the thorough recap, this is exactly what I was hoping for. A few clarifications and notes from our team:

- Confirming the incident on 2026-01-15 - attaching the internal summary (acme-incident-20260115-summary.pdf) which highlights autoscaler behavior + cache warm-up time as primary contributors.
- Our SLOs today are: p95 response <= 300ms (internal testing), availability 99.9% (monthly). We have an error budget we typically spend for feature rollouts but would like suggestions for how Redwood's fallbacks would map to our error budget.
- For graceful degradation we prefer: 1) smaller model fallback, 2) cached templated response for non-critical prompts, 3) last-known-good response as last resort. Can Redwood route by region and fall back to a different region automatically?

Questions:
1) What kind of telemetry/logs would you surface during a degradation (we need clear evidence for our incident reviews)?
2) Any limits on model variant compatibility for fallbacks (e.g., if we start with a 30B architecture, what smaller variants are supported)?

We can do Thu 26 Feb 10:00 PT for the deep-dive - Evan will join from infra.

Thanks,
Sophie
Director, Digital Products | Acme Health
Sophie.Turner@acmehealth.io

Attachment: acme-incident-20260115-summary.pdf

Chloe / Team -

Looping in a couple quick notes from the solutions side before the deep-dive:

- Telemetry: we can surface per-request routing events, model-variant traces, prefix/KV cache hit rates, and a degradation flag that marks responses served from fallback logic. Those are queryable in our Console and can be emitted as traces to your existing APM.
- Model compatibility: we typically support fallback chains across the same model family and compatible quantization; for broad cross-architecture fallbacks we recommend a short eval to validate quality under your prompts.
- For the pilot: propose a 4-week Dedicated pilot focused on the triage path with a canary rollout and automated fallback enabled.

I'll bring a Solutions Engineer and our SRE lead to the deep-dive. Marcus

Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Perfect - thanks Sophie, Evan. Confirmed Thu 26 Feb 10:00 PT for the technical deep-dive. Evan, Sophie: agenda below and a quick ask for the deep-dive to help us come prepared:

Agenda (60 min)
- 10m intros + success criteria review
- 20m infra review: current serving stack, autoscaling details, cache configuration
- 20m proposed architecture: Dedicated pilot design, fallback chain options, observability plan
- 10m next steps + mutual action plan

Ask before the call
- If possible, please share the autoscaler config (scaling thresholds) and a copy of the incident postmortem (the summary Sophie attached is great).
- Any constraints on bringing traffic to a Dedicated pool for pilot (compliance, provider restrictions).

Next immediate actions
- I uploaded the pilot proposal and the discovery notes here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-discovery (see rwi-pilot-proposal.pdf attached in original thread).
- Marcus will draft a proposed mutual-action plan after the deep-dive and share it in HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/RWI-2026-ACME-09

Thanks all - looking forward to the call.

Best,
Chloe
